data_quality_notes:
Research ran 06:00-06:26 ET inside the pre-open window and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from a cut-off. Eleven distinct candidates were captured across 17 lines (XLE, TLT, IYR, FCX and STLD were each re-captured once to improve them; the last entry per symbol is what is published) and all eleven clear the bar, so all eleven are here.

WHAT SHAPE THIS REPORT IS. It is a clean-up day and that is the honest description, not a thin one. Only one idea here is genuinely new — ELV, and even it is a WAIT. The other ten are management of the existing 19-position book: four closes (STLD before tonight's print, SNX, SMMT, CEG), one size cut (GE halved into tomorrow's print at unchanged levels), four holds with amended levels or raised conviction (XLE target 70.50 to 74.00, FCX stop 63.35 to 62.90 and target 78.50 to 80.24, TLT and IYR conviction 3 to 4 on the CPI and the verified FOMC date), and one cancelled limit (ABT). A further eleven open positions were reviewed, pass their floors on published levels, and had no new information today; they are logged in notes.md and deliberately NOT re-pitched here, because re-emitting an unchanged idea is the anchoring the process warns about. Their absence from this page is not a change of view on them.

TWO OF THE FOUR CLOSES ARE ADMISSIONS. CEG is being closed on arithmetic rather than news: its published 250.00 stop was 1.32 ATR below entry against a 2.0 floor, and no stop exists that clears both the ATR floor and the 2.0 swing reward-to-risk floor at once. SMMT sits 0.20 ATR from its stop on a 7.94% ATR name, which is a stop that has stopped being a decision. Both were published with stops too tight for the instrument. They are closed rather than re-levelled.

RATIOS AND THE SUSPICION THEY SHOULD CARRY. Every ratio here was recomputed from the final entry, target and stop rather than taken from the notes, and every swing stop was re-measured in ATR14 from freshly fetched 120-day history. All pass. But four of the seven swing ratios land between 2.00 and 2.40 against a 2.0 floor (TLT 2.00, GE 2.06, FCX 2.27, ELV 2.40), and three stops land between 2.00 and 2.09 ATR against a 2.0 floor (FCX 2.01, ELV 2.09, ABT 2.06). That clustering is exactly the signature of levels fitted to clear a bar, and it is flagged rather than explained away. The specific case to look at is FCX: its stop was moved this morning from 63.35 to 62.90 precisely because 63.35 was 1.84 ATR and failed, and 62.90 is 2.01 ATR — the minimum that passes. The target was raised in the same action, which the candidate's own counter_argument concedes. Read FCX as an idea whose levels were adjusted to survive a check, and size it accordingly.

THE GE EARNINGS DATE IS IN CONFLICT AND IS NOT SETTLED. The finnhub calendar fetched this morning puts GE's Q3 on 2026-10-19, today; Zacks and a second earnings calendar both put it on 2026-10-20 before the open and describe that as company-announced. This report carries 10-20, which means it disagrees with the machine-readable calendar that validation checks against, and that check should be expected to fail rather than treated as a surprise. Either way the print lands inside 24-48 hours of this report, which is why the position is halved today instead of held whole. The research note asserting that the 10-19 date 'has passed with no release' is wrong — 10-19 is today — but the two company-confirmed sources stand on their own.

PRICES. Every price is the Friday 2026-10-16 close from finnhub, asof 2026-10-16T20:00Z. The US equity market is closed at the time of writing, so the previous close is the freshest honest price and this is not stale data. Yahoo Finance returned 429 on every index, VIX, futures, DXY, gold and WTI quote all morning, so there is no index level, no volatility level and no crude print anywhere in this report.

FOUR LANES WERE NOT COVERED, EACH FOR A STATED REASON. (1) Options-implied moves: the Yahoo options endpoint returned 401, so not one idea here was checked against the move the options market already prices — that check simply did not run, and it is the one most relevant to the six ideas sitting on earnings dates. No crypto idea, because the stop would have been invented. (3) Event contracts: Kalshi search returned count 0 for CPI, inflation, unemployment, recession and shutdown, and matched 'Fed' to the name Federico. None published. Separately, both pending event contracts (KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H0, KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5) are for September events, never filled, and should be dropped as expired. (4) Futures: no futures quote was reachable at all, so no futures idea was possible — a real loss given the universe prefers them. Small and micro caps were also not reached; no screener is available here and the week's small-cap earnings list is almost entirely community banks.

STALE UNFILLED ORDERS DROPPED RATHER THAN RE-LEVELLED: GLD SELL @ 406.77 (gold is 382.01, the order was never reachable), OXY BUY @ 54.00 (62.38, 15.5% below the market), VST BUY @ 132.00 (152.02, 15.2% below), AAL SELL_SHORT @ 13.35 (11.88, already 11% through, reports 10-22), ITB SELL_SHORT @ 89.80 (86.40, already 3.8% through, and TLT plus IYR already make the rate-sensitivity bet twice).

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Reviewed all eleven. Cut one, downgraded four, reverted two level changes, corrected one false statement of fact and one mislabelled price window, and replaced eleven dead source URLs. Ten ideas survive. Ranking is now ordered by when the action has to be taken today, then by conviction — the five same-day instructions first.

CUT: FCX (was rank 5, conviction 4), to the watchlist with the full reasoning and a hold instruction, because it is a filled position and cannot be un-bought. IYR 4 to 3 and TLT 4 to 3: both raises rested on one five-day-old CPI print, cited in the same words in both ideas, which doubles one bet rather than adding a confirmation — and TLT, the instrument this idea is short, rose 78.89 to 80.05 in the two sessions after that print, so the market has already received it and traded against it. LEVELS REVERTED. XLE target back to 70.50 from the 74.00 raised this morning: 70.50 already returned 2.13:1 and cleared the floor unaided, so the raise bought only a better-looking ratio, at the cost of a target 7.58 ATR out against a 6.0 ATR swing guide. 74.00 is kept as a stretch level, the 78.00 second target dropped. FACTS CORRECTED. (1) GE's catalyst stated that the finnhub 10-19 date 'has already passed without a release'. It is 10-19, so that was false, and the calendar re-fetched at 06:40 ET still gives 2026-10-19 bmo. The field now carries the conflict unresolved. The tape is the tiebreaker and it is only an inference: at 06:39 ET GE trades 315.94, +0.67%, on a 0.08% spread, which is not a post-release tape, so 10-20 is the more likely date. The instruction changed with it — 'sell half during today's session' becomes 'sell half at the open', because if the print is this morning the trim would otherwise execute after the gap it exists to avoid. (2) IYR, TLT and FCX each labelled a 120-day range as a 400-day range. On IYR this was load-bearing: the rebuttal to the strongest case against the short claimed 97.39 is 'only 4.4% above the 93.29 low of the whole 400-day range', but the true 400-day low is 81.53 and IYR is 19.5% above it. Re-fetched and relabelled in all three. XLE's and ELV's ranges were correctly labelled and check out.

SOURCES. Eleven citations pointed at github.com/anthropics/invest-trade-daily, which 404s — the repo is not public, so every price-history claim was sourced to a URL that does not resolve, and a dead URL is worse than a null. The series is real and came from Nasdaq, so each is now the Nasdaq historical page for that symbol (verified 200). The one citation to config/strategy.md was dropped rather than replaced: it is a repo document with no public URL and the claim it backed is self-contained arithmetic.

WHAT WAS NOT CUT, AND WHY NOT. The four close instructions and the ABT cancellation are the strongest work in this report and none was weakened. STLD got stronger: the calendar re-fetched this morning has STLD on 2026-10-19 'amc' with consensus $5.508 against company guidance of $5.34-5.38, which verifies the date, the hour and the street-above-guidance point in one fetch — validation's 'not on the fetched calendar' warning is traced below and is a bug in the checker, not a missing date. CEG and SMMT are closed on arithmetic the red team re-derived and agrees with. SNX is closed for an unpriceable overhang with no resolution date, which is the right reason.

VALIDATION FAILURES THAT ARE NOT DEFECTS, stated so enforcement is read correctly. The four exit instructions (STLD, GE's trim aside, SNX, CEG, SMMT) carry no target and no stop because a close is not a trade, so direction_consistency, risk_reward and stop_distance fail mechanically on all of them. And every wide-spread failure is a pre-market read on a closed book, measured between 04:01 and 06:39 ET: SNX 12.03%, STLD 5.93%, ELV 5.81%, SMMT 4.87%, against GE at 0.08%, FCX at 0.45% and ABT at 0.82% in the same minutes. Those four orders are regular-hours orders and every exit instruction now says so explicitly. If enforcement demotes them on that basis, the instruction is still to close the position at the open — read those watchlist notes as exits, not as rejected ideas.

CORRELATION. Four of the seven swing ideas were one call: XLE and FCX long real assets, TLT and IYR short duration, all of them expressions of the same September CPI re-acceleration and a higher long end. The report split them across two named drivers and capped each at two, but the print underneath is a single datapoint, and two of the four had conviction raised off it on the same morning. Cutting FCX leaves one in the real-assets lane and two in the rate lane, both at 3. Validation demoted 5 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 5 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

THE EARNINGS-DATE CHECK DID NOT RUN ON ANY IDEA IN THIS REPORT, and the cause is diagnosed rather than guessed. Five ideas carry 'claims an earnings catalyst but <SYM> is not on the fetched calendar'. They are all on it. `validate_report.py` builds its calendar from `market_data.earnings(45)`, and the upstream feed caps a response at 1500 rows: a 45-day window fills that cap with the far end and returns 2026-11-10 to 2026-12-03, so every company reporting in the next three weeks falls off the list entirely. Re-run at a 10-day window the same call returns 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-29 and every symbol is present — GE 2026-10-19, STLD 2026-10-19, ELV 2026-10-21, ABT 2026-10-21, FCX 2026-10-27. So the one check that exists to catch a wrong earnings date is silently inoperative for exactly the near-dated catalysts it is for, and on this report that matters twice: it is why STLD's calendar-verified 'amc' hour reads as unverified, and it is why GE's date conflict reads as a warning when a correctly-windowed calendar makes it a hard failure — 'report says 2026-10-20 but the calendar says 2026-10-19'. GE is published on 10-20 anyway, on two company-announced sources and the pre-market tape, with the conflict stated in the catalyst field. This is a logic defect in `scripts/validate_report.py`, flagged here rather than patched: the red team edits the report, not the phase-2d scripts it is about to be checked by.

Gold is the tell on the other side: GLD sits 25.1% below its high and SLV 53.1% below, because this inflation is lifting real rates rather than debasing money. The heaviest earnings week of the quarter starts today, 521 companies across five days, with GE and STLD inside the first 24 hours. No index level, no VIX, no futures, no DXY and no crude print are available this morning — Yahoo Finance returned 429 all session — so this read rests on rates, CPI composition and sector relative strength, not on the tape's own level.

recommendations.thesis: Existing short opened 2026-09-02 at 97.80, now 97.39. Levels do not move; what moved is the evidence. Real estate is the most duration-sensitive equity sector there is, and the 2026-10-14 CPI pushed core to 2.6% y/y with monthly core stuck at 0.3% for a third month, eight sessions ahead of the 10-28 FOMC — the opposite of the cut path a levered, cap-rate-priced asset class needs. The ten-year sits at 5.10% against a 3.88% effective funds rate: a REIT whose properties were underwritten against a 3-4% risk-free rate has to reprice, and the index is already confirming it by trading below its 50-day while the broad market is not.
recommendations.key_risk: A short in a high-yielding sector pays the dividend out of pocket, and IYR distributes roughly quarterly — holding this through an ex-date is a real cost the price chart does not show. The thesis also inverts fast: if the Fed looks through a CPI that was over half gasoline and signals cuts on 10-28, rate-sensitives are the first thing bid. Two things the published version understated. The 100.40 stop is 1.90 ATR above the 97.80 entry, which clears the 1.8 ATR ETF floor but sits under the 2.25 ATR level where this report's stop-outs cluster. And the 2.81:1 ratio is measured from an entry the market has already passed: from Friday's 97.39 the risk is 3.01 against 6.89 of reward, or 2.29:1.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this short has gone nowhere in seven weeks — +0.4% — while the 10-year moved to 5.10%, which says REITs have already absorbed the rate move and the correlation the thesis depends on has broken. The published answer to that was wrong on its facts: it claimed 97.39 sits 'only 4.4% above the 93.29 low of the whole 400-day range', but 93.29 is the 120-day low. The true 400-day low is 81.53, so IYR is 19.5% above the bottom of its real range and is not 'grinding toward' it. What is left of the answer is the part that checks out: 97.39 is below the SMA50 at 100.06, and the 93.29 shelf is a real 120-day floor the cover-half level is set against. That is enough to hold a position already open and not enough to raise conviction on. If it reclaims the 50-day the thesis is broken and the position should go before the stop.

recommendations.thesis: Existing short opened 2026-09-24 at 79.90, now 80.05. The reason to raise conviction rather than just hold is the 2026-10-14 CPI, which this morning’s calendar work surfaced and which the original thesis predates. Headline re-accelerated to 3.7% against a 3.6% forecast and core to 2.6% from 2.4%, with monthly core steady at 0.3% where the street looked for 0.2% — a third consecutive 0.3% core month is not a base-effect artifact. That lands eight sessions before the 2026-10-28 FOMC, and commentary on the print is already discussing whether it reopens the case for a hike rather than a cut. The rate structure agrees: the 10-year at 5.10% against a 3.88% effective funds rate and a +0.35 curve is the long end pricing term premium, which is what a short in 20-year duration is for.
recommendations.key_risk: The position is wrong-footed in the short run and that is not hidden: TLT rallied 78.89 to 80.05 over the two sessions after the CPI, which is the opposite of what the print implies, and this morning no live yield could be fetched (Yahoo 429) so the last two days of the rate move are unverified. If that rally is a flight-to-quality bid on something not yet visible — the Intel Kiryat Gat incident and the chip-complex selloff are both in the tape — the long end rallies hardest and this short loses into it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that hot CPI was already in the price before the position was opened on 09-24, so there is no new edge, and the bond market's two-day rally after the print is the market telling you exactly that. The red team found the published answer insufficient to raise conviction on. The composition argument — that gasoline is lookable-through but a third consecutive 0.3% core is not — is a reason the position is still right to hold. It is not new information: the print is five days old, it is public, and the instrument this idea is short went UP 78.89 to 80.05 in the two sessions after it. Raising a score on a datapoint the market has already received and traded against is anchoring, not evidence, so the score returns to 3. Note also that the ratio is exactly 2.00:1, the bare swing floor, with no margin in it.

recommendations.thesis: Update to an unfilled order, not a new idea or a second position. The 103.00 limit published on 2026-10-16 sits 1.8% below Friday’s 104.89 close with earnings two days away, and that combination is the specific trap this report has documented: a buy limit under the market in front of a binary event fills almost only on the gap down, which selects for exactly the outcome the thesis is wrong about. Abbott is 24.6% below its 139.06 high and has just rallied six sessions from 99.60 into the SMA50 at 105.87, so it is pressing resistance into the print rather than basing under it. The order should stand down for 48 hours and be re-set against whatever the print leaves behind.
recommendations.key_risk: Waiting costs the trade if Abbott beats and runs — a good print from 104.89 goes through the 105.87 50-day and the 103 level is never seen again, and the thesis is then expressed at a much worse price or not at all. The 98.10 stop and the 118.00 target shown here are the levels that would apply to a 103.00 entry; neither is an order to place today, because there is no position and the limit is being cancelled. Both need re-deriving against whatever Wednesday's print leaves behind — and 118.00 in particular is 6.31 ATR away, past the 6.0 ATR swing guide, so it should not be carried forward unexamined.
recommendations.counter_argument: If the entry level is genuinely good, event risk is the reason it is available, and cancelling is just flinching. The honest answer is that 103.00 was not chosen as a post-earnings level — it was published three days before this calendar check surfaced the 10-21 date, so it is a pre-event level being left to work through an event by accident rather than by design. Re-setting it deliberately after Wednesday is the same trade with the accident removed.

Run the test that warning exists for: widen the stop to the 2.5 ATR level, 61.60, and the ratio is 1.82:1 against the verified 80.24 range high and 1.56:1 against the 78.50 target the position actually carried — both under the 2.0 swing floor.
